verdict.rationale: Clerk's own docs describe an OAuth implementation in which third-party applications request scoped access to user data, with client registration via CIMD and Dynamic Client Registration and a device authorization grant. This is direct, product-level OAuth-provider capability. However, the evidence never explicitly documents the end-to-end 'Sign in with my app' flow: OAuth application setup, the authorization-code flow, or access/ID token issuance to third parties. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of token issuance (access/ID tokens, OIDC userinfo) to third-party clients, a documented end-to-end 'Sign in with my app' / OAuth application setup guide, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can turn my own application into an OAuth provider that issues tokens to third-party clients ("Sign in with my app")

citations.quote: lets third-party applications request limited access to specific parts of a user's data through Clerk's API
Clerk supports both Client ID Metadata Documents (CIMD) and Dynamic Client Registration for OAuth client registration.
CLIs, TVs, game consoles, and other devices can ask a user to approve access from a browser-capable device without entering their credentials on the original device.
